title: How Can a Lake Kill Without Flooding?

lines.text: On an August evening in nineteen eighty-six, a lake in Cameroon released an invisible danger.
lines.spoken: On an August evening in nineteen eighty-six, a lake in Cameroon released an invisible danger.

lines.text: People did not have to touch the water.
lines.spoken: People did not have to touch the water.
lines.hero: camera moves from lake toward a schematic valley

lines.text: The danger travelled through the air.
lines.spoken: The danger travelled through the air.
lines.hero: thin shaded gas layer follows the valley floor

lines.text: More than seventeen hundred people died.
lines.spoken: More than seventeen hundred people died.
lines.hero: hold on a restrained casualty statement

lines.text: The main killer was not floodwater, fire, or a flow of lava.
lines.spoken: The main killer was not floodwater, fire, or a flow of lava.
lines.hero: three simple hazards recede, leaving the lake

lines.text: It was carbon dioxide, released from the lake itself.
lines.spoken: It was carbon dioxide, released from the lake itself.
lines.hero: lake section reveals the gas reservoir

lines.text: How can a lake make the air around it deadly?
lines.spoken: How can a lake make the air around it deadly?
lines.hero: pull back from valley to the lake and title

lines.text: The answer begins beneath a surface that hides what is happening below.
lines.spoken: The answer begins beneath a surface that hides what is happening below.
lines.hero: camera crosses the surface into the section diagram
